rows.label: Derivation
rows.text: # Greenhouse effect, global warming, climate change ## 1. Introduction Opening frame for **Greenhouse effect** — what the topic is, why it matters, a real-world hook (Nepal where possible), the map of what follows, and the learning outcomes (biology-plan.md §3.1, block I). Prose depth is written in the Environmental Issues fill pass. ## 2.…  ·  The **greenhouse effect** is natural and life-giving: CO2, CH4, water vapour and other gases let sunlight in but slow the infrared escape, keeping Earth ~33°C warmer than it would be. The problem is the **enhanced** effect: fossil fuel burning and deforestation have raised CO2 from ~280 to over 420 ppm, driving **global warming** and with it **climate change** — shifting rainfall, melting ice, rising seas.

rows.label: Shortcut
rows.text: Trick 1: Mechanism: greenhouse gases (CO2, CH4, N2O, CFCs) transmit incoming short-wave sunlight but absorb outgoing long-wave infrared → warming — the one-way valve picture.  ·  Trick 2: Gas potency: CH4 ~25× CO2 (20-yr), CFCs thousands× — quote one multiplier; CO2 dominates by volume.

rows.text: **Most-asked points (NEB).** (1) Explain the greenhouse mechanism with a diagram. (2) Distinguish the natural effect from the enhanced effect. (3) List the greenhouse gases with sources — which is most potent per molecule? (4) Mitigation vs adaptation with two examples each.…  ·  ## 8. Summary and self-check 5–10 line chapter summary, self-check questions and the common-confusions list (block VIII) — completed in the unit fill pass.  ·  **Summary.** The greenhouse effect is physics we need; the enhanced effect is the problem. CO2 dominates by volume, CH4 by potency; mitigation cuts the cause, adaptation blunts the harm. **Self-check:** can you explain why water vapour is a feedback and not a driver?
